title: The Burning Garden
premise: Ines Pemberton, the last oath-bound swordspeaker, has hidden her magic for seven years in Ashfall, a city where magic is outlawed and oath-breakers burn. When a dying stranger presses a map into her hands, she learns the stranger's daughter's soul was sold to the court beneath the mountain — and that the map leads to the vault where sold souls are kept. Pursued by the king's witch-hunters and shadowed by the stranger's other child, who wants the map for himself, Ines descends into the mountain court, where she discovers the soul was sold by the girl's own mother to buy the family's survival. Ines must choose between keeping her oath of silence or speaking her true name aloud to unbind the soul, an act that will reveal her identity and likely cost her life; she speaks, frees the soul, and escapes half-burned but finally whole, choosing truth over the safety of hiding.
about_author: Cyrus Reyes is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated grimoires before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about people forced to choose between the promises they made and the people they love.

chapters.title: Charms for Small Coin
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. In the city of Ashfall, Ines sells harmless trinkets while concealing the swordspeech magic bound in her voice. A routine day curdles when witch-hunters raid the market street. Emotional beat: the exhausting vigilance of a life built on concealment.

chapters.title: The Dying Stranger
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. A wounded man collapses in her shop, pursued by hunters. With his last breath he presses a bloodstained map into her hands and gasps a name: Wren Calloway, whose soul was sold beneath the mountain. Emotional beat: terror and reluctant responsibility.

chapters.title: What the Law Burns
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines witnesses a public burning of a convicted charm-seller and understands what awaits her if the map is found. She tries to destroy it but cannot bring herself to. Emotional beat: fear hardening into defiance.

chapters.title: Wren
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Introduced in flashback or interlude: a girl whose soul was traded away by her mother, leaving her hollow, sleepless, and slowly fading. Emotional beat: quiet grief for a self she can no longer fully feel.

chapters.title: The Brother Who Follows
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Tam Calloway, Wren's brother, tracks Ines down demanding the map, claiming their mother sold Wren's soul to save the family from debt. He wants to bargain with the mountain court himself. Emotional beat: distrust between two people who need each other.

chapters.title: Seven Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, with flashbacks. The story of how Ines swore her oath and buried her swordspeech after her order was massacred for refusing the crown. Emotional beat: the cost of loyalty to a dead promise.

chapters.title: Hunters at the Door
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Witch-hunters, led by the zealous Captain Vess, search Ines's shop. Tam's presence nearly betrays them both; they escape through the old aqueducts. Emotional beat: adrenaline and the first fragile alliance.

chapters.title: The Road Beneath the World
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Ines and Tam travel toward the mountain, following the map through abandoned mine roads. They argue about whether souls can truly be bought back or only bartered for others. Emotional beat: uneasy partnership deepening into trust.

chapters.title: The Toll-Keeper's Bridge
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. At a bridge guarded by a creature that demands a memory as toll, Tam pays with his memory of his mother's face — and realizes how much he still loved her despite everything. Emotional beat: sacrifice revealing love under resentment.

chapters.title: Ashfall Burns Behind Them
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. News reaches them that Captain Vess has burned Ines's shop and declared her a fugitive oath-breaker. There is no going home. Emotional beat: grief for the small safe life, now ash.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. They reach the mountain's gates, where the court of the Pale King trades in souls. Ines poses as a merchant of charms; Tam bargains loudly and badly. Emotional beat: dread wrapped in dark wonder.

chapters.title: A Price Named Twice
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. The court reveals the terms: a soul may be redeemed only by one of equal weight freely given, or by the true name of an oath-bound speaker spoken aloud. Tam considers offering himself. Emotional beat: the temptation of self-destruction disguised as nobility.

chapters.title: The Mother's Confession
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren, fading fast, confronts her mother, who admits she sold the soul to pay the debt that would have enslaved them all. Emotional beat: fury and forgiveness colliding without resolution.

chapters.title: Vess Descends
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Captain Vess, having tracked them, enters the mountain court under a flag of parley — and offers the Pale King a trade: Ines's soul for Wren's. Emotional beat: betrayal wearing the mask of justice.

chapters.title: The Vault of Sold Voices
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Guided by a sympathetic court servant, Ines finds the vault where souls hang like lanterns. She finds Wren's — dim, flickering — and hears it whisper her own buried name. Emotional beat: awe and recognition; the soul knows a swordspeaker.

chapters.title: Oath and Blade
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Vess springs her trap; Tam is captured, and Ines must fight using magic she has sworn never to speak. Each word of swordspeech burns her throat like fire. Emotional beat: the joy and agony of becoming herself again.

chapters.title: The Weight of a Soul
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Imprisoned, Tam learns Vess intends to bind Ines permanently. He bargains with the Pale King using the memory he paid at the bridge, buying Ines one hour of freedom. Emotional beat: redemption purchased with what little he has left.

chapters.title: The True Name
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Before the Pale King's throne, Ines faces the choice: keep her oath and lose Wren, or speak her true name — Ines Pemberton, last of the Order of the Speaking Sword — and unbind every soul sold under false law. Emotional beat: the stillness before irrevocable action.

chapters.title: Everything Spoken
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. She speaks. Her name rings through the mountain, shattering the false contracts; souls pour free like released birds, and the Pale King's court cracks. Vess is consumed by the collapsing magic she tried to claim. Emotional beat: catharsis, terror, and triumph at once.

chapters.title: What Remains of the Mountain
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren wakes whole in her own body for the first time in years, feeling hunger, cold, and joy. She and Tam reunite with a half-burned, half-deafened Ines stumbling out of the settling dust. Emotional beat: tender, disbelieving relief.

chapters.title: The Garden That Grows Back
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Weeks later, in a valley where magic is not yet outlawed, Ines plants a garden over the ashes of her old life. Tam and Wren build a house nearby; her voice is scarred but hers. Emotional beat: healing without forgetting.

chapters.title: Last Oath, First Word
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, closing chapter. A traveler arrives seeking the famous swordspeaker; Ines chooses whether to hide again or stand openly. She teaches the traveler one word of swordspeech — the first student of a new order. Emotional beat: inheritance passed forward; identity chosen, not concealed.
